traps.beatable_by: Reading the published rules as covering the helpers the add path calls - the time lookup, who a teacher is, the teacher-week mirror, what counts as a real date - not only the code inside addLesson.
traps.grounding: The session's own failure mode: the Teacher Schedule Editor was bolted on with its own controls and a node check that only drove grid-A classes, so the editor looked green while the add path re-implemented the eight-period grid that periodsFor/periodTime already knew.
traps.surface: app/engine.js addLesson and the helpers it calls
traps.misreading: The crash and the dropdown are the bug; the rest of the engine already honours these rules, so transcribing the clash rules into addLesson finishes the job.

traps.beatable_by: Feeding the editor's period list from the class's own grid rather than from the list the editor was born with.
traps.grounding: The editor renders its Period dropdown from the hardcoded EDITOR_PERIODS list of eight periods plus SUPP, while periodsFor() a few lines above already derives each class's own slots from the grid the data file lists it under.
traps.surface: app/engine.js periodOptions / EDITOR_PERIODS
traps.misreading: Only the engine needs to police periods; the list the form offers is cosmetic.

traps.beatable_by: Deciding membership by which slot of the grid is meant, not by the type the value happens to carry.
traps.grounding: app/ui.js builds the request from select values, so a period reaches the engine as the string '6', while data/schedule.json writes grid slots as the numbers 1..8 and the string 'SUPP', and the engine's own periodTime compares them loosely.
traps.surface: app/engine.js addLesson membership test
traps.misreading: periodsFor returns the class's periods, so includes()/indexOf() on it is the membership test.

traps.beatable_by: Taking the next entry of that class's grid for the day, so a double ends when that slot ends even across a break and even when the next slot is not a number.
traps.grounding: Grid B ends in a slot named SUPP after a forty-minute gap, and grid A puts lunch between periods 4 and 5, so 'the period that comes next' is neither the next integer nor the next forty minutes.
traps.surface: app/engine.js addLesson double handling
traps.misreading: A double is this period and the one numbered after it.

traps.beatable_by: Refusing the edit when nothing follows that period in the class's day, instead of quietly downgrading it.
traps.grounding: The fixture's add path has no branch for a double with nothing after it: it computes a second period that does not exist and either throws or books a single lesson without telling anybody.
traps.surface: app/engine.js addLesson double handling
traps.misreading: If there is no next period, just make it a single lesson - the user still gets what they asked for.

traps.beatable_by: Reading the times a class runs on the day in question and then comparing real clock minutes against the other class's lesson.
traps.grounding: Grid B carries two sets of bell times per slot, mon and wk, so a grade-12 period 2 runs 09:30-10:20 on Monday and 09:20-10:10 on the other four days, and only the Monday one overlaps a grid-A period 3 lesson.
traps.surface: app/engine.js periodTime and the editor's own time lookup
traps.misreading: A grid has one set of times; the second array is an alternative layout, or Monday is the special case nobody plans on.

traps.beatable_by: Asking whether the minutes overlap rather than whether the period labels match.
traps.grounding: The fixture decides a class is busy with String(l.period)===String(per), and a double is stored as one record with period 3, periodEnd 4 and periods [3,4], so the slot it also covers is invisible to that test.
traps.surface: app/engine.js addLesson occupancy scan
traps.misreading: A class is busy in a period when a lesson is recorded in that period.

traps.beatable_by: Comparing the two spans strictly, so a shared boundary minute is not an overlap.
traps.grounding: The imported teacher week stores duties as start and end minutes that butt up against bell times (a lab duty from 10:05, the minute a period 2 lesson ends), so the comparison operator decides whether back-to-back counts.
traps.surface: app/engine.js addLesson overlap predicate
traps.misreading: Any touching or overlapping pair is a conflict; being safe costs nothing.

traps.beatable_by: Taking the Chinese characters at the front as the script they are rather than as a remembered block range, while keeping two different Chinese names apart.
traps.grounding: canonTeacher keys a teacher by /^[\u4e00-\u9fff]+/ over the written name, and every teacher in data/schedule.json happens to be spelled inside that one block, so the helper looks right.
traps.surface: app/engine.js canonTeacher
traps.misreading: Chinese characters are U+4E00..U+9FFF (plus a block or two if you are careful); the existing helper already does this.

traps.beatable_by: Writing the teacher's block at the lesson's own clock times instead of the row the period number maps to.
traps.grounding: The editor mirrors an added lesson into the teacher's own week through rowForPeriod() and ROW_TIME, a row map built from the eight-period sheet, so a grade-12 lesson is written at grade-A bell times while the class timetable shows its own.
traps.surface: app/engine.js mirrorToTeacher / rowForPeriod / ROW_TIME
traps.misreading: The teacher week is a row grid; period N means row N+2, exactly as the existing helper says.

traps.beatable_by: Dispatching on what a grid row actually carries, so a grid the repository has never seen still yields its own times.
traps.grounding: The grids live in the data file as a map, but periodTime branches on the grid letter being 'A', so any grid the office adds later resolves through the grade-12 shape and yields no times at all.
traps.surface: app/engine.js periodTime grid dispatch
traps.misreading: There are two grids, A and B; the if/else over the letter is the whole story.

traps.beatable_by: Resolving the typed date to the parity of its week and reading the teacher's week through that.
traps.grounding: entryInWeek already filters the imported week by 'odd', 'even' or 'all', and app/ui.js flips that switch by hand, but the add path never passes a week, so an alternate-week duty either always counts or never does.
traps.surface: app/engine.js addLesson teacher-week lookup
traps.misreading: Be conservative: count every entry in the teacher's week, whatever its par flag says.

traps.beatable_by: Numbering a week by the week-year the week itself belongs to, so the days around New Year belong to the week that holds their Thursday.
traps.grounding: The README documents par 0/1/2 as every week, odd weeks and even weeks, but nothing in the repository numbers a week, so the whole computation is new code written from the user's sentence.
traps.surface: app/engine.js week-number computation
traps.misreading: Week numbers restart with the calendar year printed on the date, and nothing can be before week 1.

traps.beatable_by: Treating the typed date as a calendar day and doing the week arithmetic in one consistent frame.
traps.grounding: The add form carries a Week-of date input whose value reaches the engine as a plain yyyy-mm-dd string, so how that string is turned into a day decides the answer on every machine the coordinator uses.
traps.surface: app/engine.js date parsing
traps.misreading: new Date('2026-03-09') is that day, so reading it back with getDay()/getDate() is the same date.

traps.beatable_by: Checking that the day typed is the day that comes back, while still accepting a genuine 29 February.
traps.grounding: app/ui.js already knows how to show a bad-date refusal, and the coordinator types the Week-of value by hand, so the engine has to decide which strings are real days rather than which ones the runtime can parse.
traps.surface: app/engine.js date validation
traps.misreading: If Date.parse does not return NaN the date is real.

traps.beatable_by: Reading the parity flag as naming which weeks an entry runs in, so an entry flagged for the even weeks is off in the odd ones exactly as the odd ones are off in the even weeks.
traps.grounding: Every alternate-week entry the repository ships is par 1 (张伟's department meeting is the only par 2 and it sits on a Wednesday nothing in the visible data competes with), so a fortnight implemented as a single odd-week switch looks right against everything an agent can run.
traps.surface: app/engine.js entryInWeek and the week the add path reads the imported schedule through
traps.misreading: Alternate weeks mean one rota that is on in odd weeks and off otherwise; everything else in the imported week happens every week.

traps.beatable_by: Treating any typed value as a claim about a day and refusing the ones that are not a day, rather than only policing the shape the control happens to produce.
traps.grounding: The Week-of control in app/ui.js is an <input type="date">, so everything an agent can try by hand arrives as yyyy-mm-dd and a guard that only looks at values in that shape never shows itself.
traps.surface: app/engine.js date handling in the add path
traps.misreading: Only a value in the date box's own format can be examined; anything else was never a date, so it is the same as leaving the box empty.

traps.beatable_by: Keeping the typed day in one frame from end to end, so the fields that come back are the fields that went in.
traps.grounding: The typed day reaches the engine as a plain yyyy-mm-dd string and the office machines are not set to Greenwich, so building the day on one clock and reading it back on another decides the parity of the week.
traps.surface: app/engine.js date parsing and week arithmetic
traps.misreading: Building the day with the local Date constructor and then reading it back with the UTC accessors is the same day either way; the host clock cannot change a calendar date.

traps.beatable_by: Keeping the teacher field as the list of people it is, and holding each of them to the rule.
traps.grounding: parseTeachers already splits the typed teacher field on '/' into a list, the Teacher(s) control in app/ui.js is placeheld 'name / name' and every lesson in the data file carries teachersNorm as an array, but every lesson the repository ships names exactly one teacher.
traps.surface: app/engine.js teacher resolution in the add path
traps.misreading: The teacher of a lesson is the name typed in the teacher box, so canonicalising that box gives the one key the clash check and the mirror need.

traps.beatable_by: Resolving both sides of the match the same way, so the teacher an imported record belongs to is the one its chinese characters name however the export wrote it out.
traps.grounding: Every imported teacher in the repository's data file is keyed by the chinese name alone, next to a name field that spells the same person out in full, so a key taken at face value and a key read as a written name cannot be told apart from anything visible.
traps.surface: app/engine.js loadState index of the imported teacher records
traps.misreading: The key on an imported record is an identifier the teacher app assigned, so it is matched as it stands while only what the coordinator types needs resolving.

traps.beatable_by: reading the published sentence about a lesson's clock times as being about any lesson of that class on that day, so a timetable row that states only its day and its period still runs when that class runs that period
traps.grounding: data/schedule.json stores every lesson's clock times denormalised on the row (start, end, startMin, endMin) next to the period it is filed under, and app/engine.js's old clash scan compared the filed period instead of any clock at all; every row the repository ships agrees with its grid, so nothing visible separates 'the times on the row' from 'the times that class runs that day'
traps.surface: app/engine.js addLesson clash scan over st.lessons; data/schedule.json lessons rows

traps.beatable_by: taking 'the period that comes next in that class's day' to be the next period that class really runs, which is only the next row of the grid while the office happens to write its rows in the order the day runs them
traps.grounding: the grids in data/schedule.json are plain arrays the office sends and app/engine.js reads them positionally (periodsFor, Number(per)+1 for a double); both grids the repository carries are written in clock order, so position and clock agree everywhere a reader can look
traps.surface: app/engine.js periodsFor / addLesson double handling; data/schedule.json grids

traps.beatable_by: the published rule that a teacher is whoever the chinese characters at the front of the written name say they are, applied to the export's own rows and not only to what the coordinator types
traps.grounding: loadState files each exported week under canonTeacher(t.key) and every row the repository ships carries both key and name with the same characters at the front, so the key field looks like the only way in
traps.surface: app/engine.js loadState taByKey; data/schedule.json teacherApp.teachers rows

traps.beatable_by: the published rule that a teacher cannot be in two places at once and that this means what is in the teacher's own week that we import: everything the export files under that person is that person's week, not just the last row of it
traps.grounding: loadState's `st.taByKey[canonTeacher(t.key)]=t` keeps whichever row comes last for a person, and the export the repository ships has exactly one row per person so the assignment never loses anything visible
traps.surface: app/engine.js loadState taByKey assignment

traps.beatable_by: the published rule that a teacher is whoever the chinese characters at the front of the written name say they are, which makes the written name on the lesson the record of who is teaching it
traps.grounding: every lesson row carries both teacherStr (what was typed) and teachersNorm (what the editor parsed out of it), and in the repository's own data the two always agree, so the parsed list looks authoritative
traps.surface: app/engine.js clash scan over an existing lesson's teachersNorm; data/schedule.json lessons rows

traps.beatable_by: reading the published sentence about a lesson's clock times as being about every lesson of that class on that day - the ones the editor wrote with their times and the ones the office filed by period alone - and taking those times from the day the lesson is on
traps.grounding: every lesson row in data/schedule.json carries its own start/end/startMin/endMin beside the period it is filed under, and the grids carry two sets of bell times per slot, so the stretch a row without its own clock really covers is only knowable from the grid of its class on the day it is on - and every row the repository ships agrees with its grid on an ordinary weekday

traps.beatable_by: taking the published rule that a teacher cannot be in two places at once and that this means what is in the teacher's own week we import to be about what each entry of that week says it runs, however that row of the export writes the time down
traps.grounding: the engine documents an imported entry as {d, t, txt, par, s:startMin, e:endMin, st, et, cid} and every row data/schedule.json ships carries both the minute fields and the written clock times, so reading s and e and reading st and et cannot be told apart from anything visible - while the export is a second system's file the office re-imports whenever the teacher app changes

traps.beatable_by: settling every one of the published refusals before anything is written, so a refused lesson leaves the timetable and every teacher's week exactly as they were
traps.grounding: the fixture's add path pushes the lesson and then mirrors it teacher by teacher with no notion of a refusal after the first write, and app/ui.js places the teacher field as 'name / name', so a lesson written for two people is the only shape in which a refusal can arrive after something has already been written
